claim: Demand for self-owned, local AI memory has spilled beyond geeks. In the Show HN thread for Echologue (a privacy-first AI voice journal), one commenter reports: "I got tired of my stuff living on someone else's server, so I ended up building my own local memory thing. Not a developer at all, just stubborn." Another user's first request is BYOK so they control where inference happens. First-hand demand evidence for the "your context lives with you, locally" lane; the nameable gap is that every current option still assumes a technical user willing to self-host.
method: HN Algolia 48h Show HN sweep + comment mining via items API (pain-point verbatims).

voices.quote: I got tired of my stuff living on someone else's server, so I ended up building my own local memory thing. Not a developer at all, just stubborn.
I just tried the android application, really like the privacy first approach. Would you consider adding BYOK so that a user could have complete control over where inference happens?

does: A demand signal rather than a repo: in the Show HN thread for Echologue (privacy-first AI voice journal), a self-described non-developer reports building his own local memory tool out of privacy frustration, and another user's first request is BYOK control over where inference happens.
why_use: First-hand proof that 'my AI context should live with me, locally' has escaped the geek bubble.
gap: All current local AI memory options assume technical self-hosting, leaving non-developers without a simple, private alternative.
counter: Platform memory (ChatGPT/Claude/Google) is free, default-on and zero-effort; teaching ordinary users to own their memory store is an uphill education fight.
differentiator: Ship a no-server, no-account personal memory vault as a consumer app, importing chat exports and voice notes; privacy is the entire pitch. Cold start: EN — the Echologue HN thread and r/PrivacyGuides; CN — 小红书'AI 日记 隐私'笔记评论区.
value: The context-lock-in fight (flagged by a16z) makes user-owned memory a real category; journal/voice memory for privacy buyers is the wedge.
risk: Category education cost is high and platforms can bundle 'export+local mode' any time.

zh.claim: 自持本地 AI 记忆的需求已经外溢出极客圈：Echologue 的 Show HN 帖里，一位自称非开发者的用户因为受不了数据放在别人服务器上，自己动手搭了本地记忆工具。
zh.does: 这是需求信号而非项目：Echologue（隐私优先的 AI 语音日记）的 Show HN 帖里，非开发者自述动手搭了自己的本地记忆工具；另一位用户的第一个要求就是 BYOK、自己决定推理在哪跑。
zh.why_good: 这是需求信号而非项目：Echologue（隐私优先的 AI 语音日记）的 Show HN 帖里，非开发者自述动手搭了自己的本地记忆工具；另一位用户的第一个要求就是 BYOK、自己决定推理在哪跑。
zh.why_use: '我的 AI 上下文应该跟着我、放在本地'这件事第一次有了圈外普通人的一手证据。
zh.gap: 现有的自持记忆方案全部默认你是愿意自托管的技术用户，而正在开口要的人明说自己不是开发者。
zh.counter: 平台记忆（ChatGPT/Claude/Google）免费、默认开启、零成本；教育普通用户自己管记忆库是场硬仗。
zh.differentiator: 做一个无服务器、无账号的个人记忆保险箱消费级应用，导入聊天记录和语音笔记，隐私就是全部卖点。冷启动：英文蹲 Echologue 帖和 r/PrivacyGuides；中文蹲小红书'AI 日记 隐私'笔记评论区。
zh.value: a16z 点名的'上下文锁定'之争让用户自持记忆成为真品类；隐私买家的日记/语音记忆是切口。
zh.risk: 品类教育成本高，且平台随时可以捆绑'导出+本地模式'。
zh.hook: 受够了数据放在别人服务器上的非开发者——宁可自己粗糙地搭一个，也不愿不搭。

hook: Non-developers who are fed up enough with their data living on someone else's server that they are building their own memory tools badly rather than not at all.
consumer_angle: An ordinary person can own their AI memory without touching a server, just like using a private journal that never leaves their device.
pick_reason: Pain is verified by non-developer quotes, but the gap is still a niche and the wedge requires building a polished consumer product.
